summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any gain a taxpayer receives from the government taking their property through eminent domain, including sales made under threat of such action.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude certain gains from gross income, specifically those from property converted by eminent domain. This change would result in lower taxes for affected individuals, making taxation a central theme of the bill.

The bill creates a new tax exclusion under IRC section 139M for gains realized from property taken by eminent domain, directly reducing federal tax revenue. Because the entire legislation is devoted to enacting this revenue-losing provision, it has a clear, central effect of increasing the deficit.
